title: ChatGPT and generative artificial intelligence: an exploratory study of key benefits and challenges in operations and supply chain management
explain_beginner: This paper asked supply chain professionals in the United States and United Kingdom how they use ChatGPT and similar generative AI. It found that projects range from small early tests to full deployment. Most aim at practical improvements, such as happier customers, lower costs, and smoother processes. The biggest difficulties involve information, technology, and company organisation. People expect lower spending, better customer experiences, more automated work, and environmental gains. Industries fall into six clusters based on the benefits and obstacles they see. The work matters because it gives companies a clearer picture of how mature these projects are and what they might face.
explain_business: This study suggests generative AI in supply chains is moving from experiments toward broader use, but adoption is uneven. Executives should expect near term value mainly from customer service, cost control, and process improvement. Barriers are not only tools, they include data quality, technology fit, and organizational readiness. Longer term upside includes automation and sustainability. Because industries fall into six groups based on perceived benefits and obstacles, leaders can compare their sector's outlook. The decision this informs is how to stage investment, where to strengthen foundations, and how to judge project maturity honestly rather than overstate progress.
explain_practitioner: The authors surveyed 300 supply chain respondents, 119 in the United States and 181 in the United Kingdom, about current generative AI projects and perceptions. They examined where efforts sit on a maturity spectrum from initial trials to complete rollout. Reported gains centered on happier customers, lower costs, and smoother processes. Barriers involved information quality, technical fit, and company setup. Expected outcomes included lower spending, better customer interactions, more automated work, and environmental responsibility. The study grouped industries into six clusters based on perceived advantages and rollout obstacles. Its key result is a structured map of advantages, obstacles, future expectations, and project readiness for generative AI in supply chain work.
